html:
Performers
Pierre Bernac (baritone), Francis Poulenc (piano) Documented

The Internet Archive item credits Pierre Bernac and Francis Poulenc and lists baritone and piano; the March 1948 supplement names both and cites “the composer’s participation in the recording”.

[1] [2]
Work version
Songs 7, 8 and 9 of the nine-song cycle for voice and piano, on the third side of the set. Documented

The Internet Archive item lists the three songs on this side in this order. The dealer’s supplement lists the nine songs and says the cycle occupies three sides. The printed edition used is not named.

[1] [2]
Recorded
Not stated Unknown

The set was listed as an import by March 1948. The Internet Archive metadata for the other two sides of the set gives “1948-12”, which is later than that listing and so cannot be the date of recording or first issue.

[1] [2]
Place
Not stated Unknown

No source consulted names the studio.

[1]
Label
His Master’s Voice (HMV), 12-inch 78 rpm Documented

The supplement lists two 12-inch imported records, Nos. G-DB6383/4.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
DB 6384, side 1 (the cycle’s first six songs are on the two sides of DB 6383) Documented

The Internet Archive label data read “D.B.6384” for this side, with Dans le jardin d’Anna on the other; the other transfers of the set read “D.B.6383”.

[1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
2EA 11110-1 (this side); the reverse, Dans le jardin d’Anna, is 2EA 11131 Documented

From the item descriptions of the two transfers.

[1]
Transfer
George Blood, L.P., for the Great 78 Project (Internet Archive); disc from the Goodfriend collection Documented

The item description names the engineer’s firm and lists the collections georgeblood and 78rpm_goodfriend.

[1]
Transfer date
Not stated; the item was made public on 1 July 2024 Unknown

The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

[1]
Processing
Four stylus sizes were tried; the preferred version was equalised with turnover 375 Hz and roll-off −12 dB, and copied under the friendlier file name. Documented

As stated in the item description. The published MP3 is the Internet Archive derivative of that file.

[1]
Composition rights
Poulenc died in 1963, so the music is in copyright in the EU under the life-plus-70 term, which runs to the end of 2033; national wartime extensions, which can lengthen the term for older works in France, were not assessed. The poems are by Paul Éluard, who died in 1952; rights in the poems are not assessed here. Documented

Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording. The dates of death are those given in the cited note; the United States status of the music and the poems is not established here.

[3]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; listed as an import by March 1948. Documented

The United States status of a recording made in France in the 1940s is not established.

[2]

Francis Poulenc, Tel jour telle nuit, FP 86, songs 7–⁠9. Pierre Bernac, baritone; Francis Poulenc, piano. HMV DB 6384, listed as an import by March 1948. Transfer by George Blood, L.P., for the Great 78 Project; Internet Archive item 78_tel-jour-telle-nuit-no-3_pierre-bernac-francis-poulenc-poulenc_gbia0553972a. Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established. Rights statement

  1. Internet Archive — TEL JOUR TELLE NUIT No. 3 (Pierre Bernac & Francis Poulenc): metadata and file inventory — metadata.description (songs a–c, matrix 2EA11110-1, catalogue D.B.6384, stylus and equalisation note), collections georgeblood and 78rpm_goodfriend; file TEL JOUR TELLE NUIT No. 3 - PIERRE BERNAC & FRANCIS POULENC.mp3 (4:46). The companion items for the other sides give matrices 2EA11108-2 and 2EA11109-1 (D.B.6383) and 2EA11131 (Dans le jardin d’Anna). Accessed 2026-10-19.
  2. The Gramophone Shop Supplement, March 1948 (Internet Archive scan) — Entry “POULENC: Tel jour, tel nuit — Song Cycle (3 sides) & Dans le Jardin d’Anna (1 side) … Two 12-inch imported records, Nos. G-DB6383/4; price $5.24”, with the nine song titles. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  3. Graham Johnson — note on Tel jour telle nuit, FP 86, Hyperion CDH55366 — Composition at Noizay and Lyon, December 1936 to January 1937; the dedicatees; Éluard’s four proposed titles; Éluard’s dates 1895–⁠1952 in the page header. Accessed 2026-10-19.
  4. John Check — “Poulenc’s voice”, review of Roger Nichols, Poulenc: A Biography, The New Criterion, 21 May 2020 — Paragraph on “Nous avons fait la nuit”: the leap on “Je ris encore” and the piano postlude after “toujours nouveau”. Accessed 2026-10-19.
